purpose: Portfolio-specific shadow discovery for fresh company, sector and geopolitical hooks not already covered by canonical Live Market Motion. It cannot establish upstream priority or change company scores by itself.

policy.role: Shadow discovery only. Canonical Live Market Motion is consumed first; local items exist only to fill uncovered portfolio-specific hooks.
policy.sourceRule: Yahoo Finance/Reuters may be used for discovery and current reporting. Material claims that could alter a score or capital-allocation gate require company/official/primary confirmation.
policy.scoreRule: A motion item cannot change Base Conviction or a fundamental score by itself.
policy.expiryRule: Local discovery uses the same 48-hour freshness horizon as Live Motion. Older items are archive/context unless a genuinely new development refreshes the event.
policy.politicalRule: Political and geopolitical items remain factual/attributed and are used only for market transmission, not political judgement.
policy.focusRule: Legacy primary/secondary buckets are storage history only. Presentation must not infer a three-item primary quota or competing editorial rank from them; render uncovered local discovery as one downstream pool.
policy.legacyBucketRule: The primary/secondary arrays are retained for compatibility during migration only and must be flattened before presentation or portfolio routing.

primary.headline: Micron earnings become the cleanest live test of the memory-scarcity thesis
primary.whatHappened: Micron is scheduled to report fiscal fourth-quarter results after the September 30 close, with the market focused on DRAM, HBM pricing, supply growth and AI-driven demand.
primary.whyInteresting: Expectations are already very high, so the stock reaction can be more informative than the headline numbers. Strong operating evidence with a weak tape would create a useful expectation-versus-reaction divergence.
primary.bigPictureBridge: AI workloads → HBM/DRAM demand → memory pricing/supply → earnings and guidance → semiconductor breadth.
primary.powerStackUse: Use the result to update memory/AI hardware research only after the actual release. Compare guidance with the stock reaction instead of treating an earnings beat as automatic confirmation.
primary.hybridAngle: If memory scarcity is genuinely as tight as the thesis says, Micron should be able to show it in pricing, margins and forward commentary; the market's reaction tells us whether that was already priced.
primary.linkedTheme: US–China AI War / AI Abundance + Compute Sovereignty

primary.headline: Iran says it received a U.S. response to its trust-building proposal
primary.whatHappened: Iranian officials said they received U.S. feedback through Qatari mediators on a seven-day trust-building proposal. Reuters reported that current disagreement centres on sequencing, including steps tied to reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
primary.whyInteresting: This is a fast-moving sentence-level catalyst for the energy complex because the negotiation path changes the probability of freer Hormuz traffic before inventories or company earnings change.
primary.bigPictureBridge: U.S.–Iran diplomacy → Hormuz shipping probability → crude/products/freight → inflation expectations → yields/USD → portfolio energy exposure.
primary.powerStackUse: Use as a macro-to-portfolio bridge for energy holdings and refiners. Do not infer a deal or supply normalisation until physical-flow evidence changes.
primary.hybridAngle: The oil story can change on diplomacy before barrels move; the key test is whether tanker flows, product cracks and freight actually follow.
primary.linkedTheme: Refined Products / Diesel Inflation + Middle East Supply Risk

primary.headline: Meta pushes into enterprise AI and hires MongoDB CEO to lead it
primary.whatHappened: Meta launched Meta Enterprise Platform around Muse, business agents, APIs and coding tools, and appointed MongoDB CEO Chirantan Desai to run the new unit.
primary.whyInteresting: This turns Meta's AI buildout into a direct monetisation test against established enterprise-software vendors rather than only a consumer-advertising or infrastructure story.
primary.bigPictureBridge: AI capex → enterprise monetisation → cash return on infrastructure spending → software competitive pressure.
primary.powerStackUse: Use as a motion hook inside AI financing/ROIC and enterprise-software research. Do not treat competitor share-price moves as proof of durable market-share loss.
primary.hybridAngle: Meta spent heavily to build the stack; now the question is whether it can turn that infrastructure into a new recurring enterprise revenue stream.
primary.linkedTheme: AI Credit / Financing Dispersion + Realizable MW

secondary.headline: Nvidia adds $150B to its buyback authorisation
secondary.whatHappened: Nvidia authorised an additional $150 billion of share repurchases, taking remaining authorisation to $235 billion through fiscal 2028. The company also announced an open platform aimed at AI-agent safety.
secondary.whyInteresting: It creates a sharp contrast inside the AI theme: Nvidia can fund expansion while returning extraordinary amounts of capital, while parts of the wider AI buildout are increasingly judged on financing quality and cash conversion.
secondary.bigPictureBridge: AI infrastructure demand → cash generation → capital return versus AI project financing stress elsewhere.
secondary.powerStackUse: Use NVDA as the cash-generation benchmark when comparing AI infrastructure names, sponsors and project-finance risk.
secondary.hybridAngle: The AI boom is not one financing story: Nvidia is returning capital at record scale while weaker projects still face a much higher hurdle rate.
secondary.linkedTheme: AI Credit / Financing Dispersion + Realizable MW

secondary.headline: Tesla Cybercab faces a federal certification deadline
secondary.whatHappened: NHTSA asked Tesla to explain by September 30 how Cybercab was self-certified under federal safety standards despite lacking conventional driver controls. The inquiry itself has not established a violation.
secondary.whyInteresting: Tesla's autonomy thesis now has a concrete regulatory scale gate, while its core vehicle-delivery outlook is also under scrutiny.
secondary.bigPictureBridge: Physical AI narrative → legal/regulatory deployment gate → fleet scaling → future revenue dependence.
secondary.powerStackUse: Keep TSLA's autonomy upside separate from verified vehicle/storage economics. Treat the regulatory response as a catalyst, not a score change until there is a material business consequence.
secondary.hybridAngle: For Tesla, the next autonomy question is not just whether Cybercab works; it is whether the product can clear the regulatory path needed to scale.

secondary.headline: Robinhood is rolling out agentic AI trading accounts
secondary.whatHappened: Robinhood said it will begin rolling out AI-agent-led trading accounts, alongside plans for weekend equity trading and other active-trader products.
secondary.whyInteresting: This is a practical market-structure story: AI is moving from research assistance toward autonomous retail execution.
secondary.bigPictureBridge: AI agents → retail trading behaviour → brokerage engagement → market microstructure and platform economics.
secondary.powerStackUse: Track as a fintech/market-structure theme seed. No score effect without evidence on adoption, economics and risk controls.
secondary.hybridAngle: AI is moving from helping people choose trades to placing them, which could change both brokerage economics and retail behaviour.

secondary.headline: Boeing wins the U.S. Navy's next-generation fighter development contract
secondary.whatHappened: The Pentagon awarded Boeing a roughly $20 billion contract to develop the Navy's F/A-XX next-generation fighter.
secondary.whyInteresting: It gives Boeing another major defence growth vector separate from the commercial-aircraft recovery and links directly to strategic aerospace spending.
secondary.bigPictureBridge: Strategic competition → defence procurement → aerospace backlog/capacity → company execution.
secondary.powerStackUse: Treat as a defence/aerospace catalyst and research lead. Future production economics and execution still determine company-level impact.
secondary.hybridAngle: Boeing's story is no longer only commercial-aircraft repair; defence backlog is becoming a second operating narrative.
secondary.linkedTheme: Critical Minerals / Rare Earth / Copper Supply Security

secondary.headline: Mortgage-score pricing parity hits FICO's moat
secondary.whatHappened: FHFA changes put VantageScore on the same mortgage pricing framework as Classic FICO for Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, and FICO shares fell sharply.
secondary.whyInteresting: It is a clean example of policy plumbing becoming company-specific moat risk in a single announcement.
secondary.bigPictureBridge: Housing policy/infrastructure → lender workflow → scoring competition → pricing power and company moat.
secondary.powerStackUse: Use as a special-situations research example and as a reminder that regulation can change competitive economics without a macro regime shift.
secondary.hybridAngle: The interesting part is not simply the share-price drop; it is how a rule change can rapidly reprice a business model that looked structurally entrenched.
secondary.linkedTheme: Global Duration / Capital Scarcity + Energy-Inflation Feedback

secondary.headline: OPEC+ is expected to keep November output targets steady
secondary.whatHappened: Reuters reported that key OPEC+ producers are expected to maintain current November production targets at Sunday's meeting.
secondary.whyInteresting: It provides a useful counterweight to the diplomacy narrative: geopolitical de-escalation would not automatically imply a large new OPEC supply response.
secondary.bigPictureBridge: Producer policy + Gulf export recovery → crude balance → products/freight → inflation and energy-equity margins.
secondary.powerStackUse: Use alongside physical export, refinery and product-market evidence rather than as a standalone directional oil signal.
secondary.hybridAngle: Even if diplomacy improves, supply policy and product tightness can keep the energy story from normalising immediately.
secondary.linkedTheme: Refined Products / Diesel Inflation + Middle East Supply Risk

secondary.headline: AstraZeneca commits $2B to Summit Therapeutics
secondary.whatHappened: AstraZeneca agreed to invest $2 billion in Summit Therapeutics and collaborate on cancer-drug combinations involving ivonescimab.
secondary.whyInteresting: It is a clean strategic-validation event with a cross-border biotech angle rather than another AI or energy story.
secondary.bigPictureBridge: External validation + balance-sheet capital → clinical-development optionality → biotech competitive landscape.
secondary.powerStackUse: Keep as special-situations discovery unless healthcare becomes a higher-priority Power Stack branch.
secondary.hybridAngle: Sometimes the most useful signal is another industry's willingness to write a very large cheque for access to a differentiated asset.
